title: AhpPairwiseMatrix
description: The complete AHP (Analytic Hierarchy Process) comparison structure for one analysis: a top-level matrix comparing the 5 clusters against each other, plus one matrix per cluster comparing that cluster's member criteria against each other. Each matrix carries its raw pairwise judgments (Saaty 1-9 scale) and the computed eigenvector weights and consistency ratio. A criterion's final weight = its cluster's weight (from cluster_comparison) × its weight within that cluster (from within_cluster_comparisons). See SPEC.md, 'AHP Pairwise Matrix' for the consistency-ratio formula and the standard random-index table.

saatyValue.description: A pairwise comparison value on Saaty's 1-9 scale, or its reciprocal (1/9 .. 1). 1 = equal importance, 9 = extreme importance of the row item over the column item, 1/9 = extreme importance of the column item over the row item. Conventionally chosen from {1/9, 1/8, ..., 1/2, 1, 2, ..., 9}.

pairwiseMatrix.description: One n×n pairwise comparison matrix plus its derived AHP results.

items.description: Ordered ids of the things being compared — either the 5 cluster names (for the top-level matrix) or criterion ids within one cluster (for a within-cluster matrix). Row/column order of 'matrix' follows this list.

matrix.description: n×n matrix of raw pairwise judgments, n = length of 'items'. matrix[i][j] expresses how much more important items[i] is than items[j] on the Saaty scale. Must be reciprocal (matrix[i][j] == 1 / matrix[j][i]) and have 1s on the diagonal.

weights.description: Principal eigenvector of 'matrix', normalized to sum to 1, in the same order as 'items'. This is the relative-priority output of the AHP calculation for this matrix.

consistency_index.description: CI = (λmax − n) / (n − 1), where λmax is the matrix's principal eigenvalue and n is its size.

random_index.description: RI, Saaty's average random-consistency index for an n×n matrix, looked up from the standard table (see SPEC.md).

consistency_ratio.description: CR = CI / RI. By AHP convention CR < 0.10 is considered acceptably consistent; CR >= 0.10 flags that the underlying judgments should be revisited.

cluster_comparison.description: The top-level 5×5 matrix comparing the 5 clusters (Topographic, Hydrological, Land Use, Infrastructure, Exposure) against each other. 'items' must be exactly those 5 cluster names.

within_cluster_comparisons.description: One pairwise matrix per cluster, keyed by cluster name, comparing that cluster's member criteria against each other.

final_weights.description: Final AHP weight per criterion id: cluster_comparison weight for that criterion's cluster × its weight within within_cluster_comparisons[cluster]. Values should sum to 1 across all criteria in the analysis. This is the same value written back onto Criterion.weight.
